descriptor.scene: ABSOLUTELY NO MARCUS IN THIS PICTURE. A plain church office in the evening. A WOMAN IN HER SIXTIES in a cardigan sits at a cluttered desk, side-on to the viewer, TALKING at length and using her hands, mid-story. She is an ordinary parish volunteer, warm and unhurried, and she has plainly been at it a while: a cold cup of tea, her coat still over the back of the chair. In front of her the laptop GLOWS DEEP INDIGO. Inside it STORYWELL stands square and still, LISTENING, head slightly inclined toward her, doing nothing else at all. The picture is about being listened to. NO ORANGE ANYWHERE. THE LAPTOP IS WHOLLY HOLOGRAPHIC AND THIS IS THE THING TO GET RIGHT: the ENTIRE machine, its lid AND its screen frame AND its keyboard AND its base AND its hinge AND its edges, is ONE single translucent luminous object made of light, glowing all the way through, so you can SEE THROUGH the whole thing to the desk and the room behind it. NO PART of it is solid, opaque, dark, grey, brown, black, metal or plastic. It has NO SOLID BASE and NO SOLID LID. It is NOT an ordinary laptop with a bright screen, and it is NOT a floating screen with no body: the whole clamshell is present and the whole clamshell is made of glowing light. It casts warm light onto the desk rather than shadow.
